title: How Caption Color Perception Shapes News Value Judgments
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how caption hue (Open Caption Telop, OCT) shapes the evaluation of news value, including credibility, novelty, and timeliness, across affective contexts. Using controlled hue manipulations based on the Practical Color Coordinate System (PCCS), participants evaluated realistic news stimuli with a continuous rating scale. Results revealed significant main effects of hue and interactions with context across all value dimensions. Warm hues enhanced perceived credibility and timeliness, particularly in negative contexts, whereas purple selectively increased perceived novelty. Intermediate hues showed less stable effects. Furthermore, certain hues facilitated integration across value dimensions, while others produced dissociative patterns. These findings demonstrate that hue functions not only as an affective cue but also as an organizing principle in evaluative judgment.
